channel.title: ICU Scope
channel.description: Daily-updated ICU/critical-care literature and FOAMed, organized by organ system.

item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Erratum: AASLD Practice Guidance on Acute-on-chronic liver failure and the management of critically ill patients with cirrhosis.
Diabetic ketoacidosis induced by long-acting growth hormone in a child without preexisting diabetes.
item.description: A 13-year-old boy developed severe diabetic ketoacidosis after starting long-acting growth hormone therapy, despite having no pre-existing diabetes. The condition resolved with insulin and fluid therapy. The case highlights the potential for growth hormone therapy to cause insulin resistance and diabetic ketoacidosis.

item.title: Point-of-Care Echocardiography in Pediatric and Neonatal Care.
item.description: This review discusses the use of point-of-care echocardiography in pediatric and neonatal care, highlighting its ability to quickly assess cardiac function and guide management decisions. POCE is a focused tool for bedside evaluation, unlike comprehensive echocardiography. It helps clinicians make rapid time-sensitive decisions.

item.title: Postinsertion care practices for nontunnelled dialysis catheters in intensive care: A cross-sectional survey.
item.description: Australian critical care nurses were surveyed about their postinsertion care practices for non-tunnelled dialysis catheters. The survey found variability in practices, with common methods including inspecting insertion sites, using chlorhexidine gluconate-impregnated dressings, and securing catheters with sutures. Troubleshooting methods also varied.

item.title: Risk Factors and Development of a Clinical Prediction Model for Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Bacteremia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: Researchers analyzed 895 patients with Enterobacterales bacteremia to identify risk factors for carbapenem resistance and predictors of mortality. They found that ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and prior carbapenem exposure increased the risk of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) bacteremia. Patients with CRE bacteremia had higher 28-day mortality rates compared to those with susceptible bacteria.

item.title: Plasma versus Whole Blood Multiplex Droplet Digital PCR for Pathogen Detection in ICU Patients with Clinically Suspected Sepsis: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
item.description: Researchers compared plasma and whole-blood tests for detecting pathogens in ICU patients with suspected sepsis. Both tests found more pathogens than traditional blood culture, but whole-blood tests detected more Candida infections. The results suggest both tests can complement blood culture.

item.title: Fosfomycin as an adjunctive agent against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii: an updated narrative review.
item.description: This study reviewed 48 studies on using fosfomycin to treat carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections. Fosfomycin may help when combined with other antibiotics, especially sulbactam, imipenem, and colistin. However, its independent contribution to treatment outcomes is unclear.

item.title: The Self-Perceived Role 2 Preparedness of Family Medicine Physicians.
item.description: This study surveyed 298 Family Medicine physicians about their preparedness to deliver Role 2 care in combat settings. Most had little experience and felt unprepared, but those with more experience and training felt more confident. Factors associated with perceived preparedness included career Role 2 experience, recent training, and caring for critically ill patients.

item.title: A Field Guide to Evidence Based Medicine Podcast – Episode 1
item.description: This podcast is the first episode of a new series on evidence-based medicine in emergency medicine, hosted by Rory and Jerry Hoffman.

item.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting subsyndromal delirium in critically ill patients in the emergency department.
item.description: Researchers developed a tool to predict the risk of subsyndromal delirium in critically ill patients in the emergency department, using six easily available clinical variables. The tool showed excellent accuracy and can help identify patients at risk early on. This can lead to targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes.

item.title: EMCrit 430 – Questions and Answers (Members Q&A Episode 004) with Sara Crager
item.description: Dr. Sarah Crager discusses bedside shock management, moving beyond blood pressure targets to a dynamic approach. They address clinical dilemmas, including lactated Ringer's in lactic acidosis and albumin and diuretics in edematous patients. A real-world approach to fluid management is explored.

item.title: Combined metabolic risk and admission lactate-to-bicarbonate ratio in critically ill children: a retrospective pediatric ıntensive care cohort study.
item.description: This study in critically ill children found that those with both high lactate and acidosis at admission were at higher risk of death and needed more organ support. A new risk classification system using both factors may help doctors quickly identify high-risk patients. The study also found that lactate levels alone can be a useful marker of risk, but should be used alongside other measures.

item.title: Tooth brushing versus routine oral care impact on ventilator-associated pneumonia in PICU: a clinical trial.
item.description: This study compared toothbrushing with chlorhexidine to routine oral care in 118 children on ventilators in the PICU. While there was no significant difference in ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) incidence, there was a trend towards reduced VAP and improved outcomes in the toothbrushing group. The study suggests that enhanced oral hygiene may be beneficial in the PICU.

item.title: Early Identification of Recovery Potential After Acute Brain Injury Using Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy.
item.description: Researchers used a non-invasive brain imaging technique called functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to predict recovery in 33 patients with acute brain injury. The fNIRS-based model accurately predicted 6-month outcomes in 81.3% of patients, outperforming clinical models. The model also predicted recovery of behavioral responsiveness in 78.5% of patients.

item.title: Weight-adjusted fluid balance and its impact on days alive without life support in critical illness - an observational cohort study.
item.description: This study of 17,956 ICU patients found that a positive fluid balance of +7% or higher and a negative fluid balance of -4% or lower were associated with fewer days alive without life support. These thresholds were linked to worse outcomes, including increased mortality, need for organ support, and delirium. The study suggests that fluid balance is a crucial factor in ICU care.

item.title: Development of a population-level frfailty index using Quebec administrative data: a Canadian retrospective study.
item.description: Researchers developed a 30-item frailty index using Quebec administrative data to identify frail ICU patients. They found that frail patients were older, more likely to have dialysis on admission, and had a higher risk of in-hospital mortality. The index showed a strong correlation between frailty and mortality.

item.title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Continuous Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict acute kidney injury in ICU patients with atrial fibrillation, using data from 19,347 patients. The model, which combines electronic health record data, achieved high accuracy in predicting AKI risk. Clinicians can use this model to inform patient management decisions.

item.title: Glycemic Ratio Is a Superior Predictor of Mortality Compared With Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio in Critically Ill Patients.
item.description: This study compared two ways to predict mortality in critically ill patients: using a single blood glucose measurement at admission, and using a ratio of mean ICU blood glucose to estimated preadmission blood glucose. The study found that the ratio method was a better predictor of mortality. The best outcome was associated with a mean ICU blood glucose level that was 80-100% of the patient's preadmission level.

item.title: A Study in Priors
item.description: Researchers found that nearly half of positive medical trial results cannot be replicated, highlighting issues with trust in medical literature.

item.title: Comparative performance of 24G and 26G short peripheral catheters in neonates: a single-centre retrospective cohort study in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit.
item.description: Researchers compared 24G and 26G short peripheral catheters in neonates and found that 26G catheters had a slightly longer dwell time and higher first-attempt insertion success rates, but similar complication rates.

item.title: Regional Citrate Anticoagulation Versus No Anticoagulation During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in Critically Ill Patients at High Risk of Bleeding: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: This meta-analysis compared regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) to no anticoagulation (NA) during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in critically ill patients at high risk of bleeding. RCA prolonged filter lifespan and reduced circuit clotting, but increased risks of citrate accumulation and hypocalcemia. RCA also reduced major bleeding events, but did not affect in-hospital mortality.

item.title: Paediatric Intubation Checklist
item.description: A checklist was developed to standardize pediatric intubation procedures, covering preparation, equipment selection, and post-intubation care.

item.title: Metabolomic Signatures of Biotrauma Associated with Mortality in ICU Patients Requiring Invasive Mechanical Ventilation and ECMO.
item.description: This study analyzed blood samples from ICU patients on invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) to identify biomarkers associated with mortality. They found distinct metabolomic signatures in patients on IMV, but not as clear in ECMO patients. These findings suggest that integrated omics analysis could be useful for predicting ICU outcomes.

item.title: Effects of nutritional therapy on morphofunctional outcomes in critically ill patients: a systematic narrative synthesis.
item.description: This review of 29 studies found that high-protein nutritional strategies and supplementation with β-hydroxy-β-methyl butyrate can help preserve muscle mass and strength in critically ill patients. However, physical function showed less responsiveness to interventions. Multimodal approaches may be needed for functional recovery.

item.title: Feeding or Failing? Rethinking Nutrition Therapy in Pediatric Critical Care.
item.description: This review examined the importance of nutrition in pediatric ICU patients, highlighting the need for early enteral nutrition and individualized strategies to meet metabolic demands.

item.title: A Cross-sectional Study to Examine the Prognostic Value of Glycated Hemoglobin Levels and Glycated Hemoglobin-adjusted Glycemic Variables in Patients with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
item.description: This study examined the relationship between glycated hemoglobin levels and glycemic variables in patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. It found that HbA1c-adjusted glycemic indices, such as glycemic gap and stress hyperglycemia ratio, were strong predictors of clinical outcomes. These indices may be useful in predicting patient outcomes and guiding treatment decisions.

item.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Adult ICU Patients: A Meta-Analysis on Its Clinical Effectiveness.
item.description: This study analyzed 22 clinical trials with 1,396 patients to compare the effectiveness of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) versus conventional blood glucose monitoring in ICU patients. CGM was found to reduce hypoglycemic events, average blood glucose levels, and daily insulin use, while also improving time in glycemic target range and reducing total mortality. These results suggest that incorporating CGM into ICU glycemic control strategies could be beneficial.

item.title: Pressure-targeted neurocritical care at the bedside: the emerging role of transcranial doppler.
item.description: This study discusses using transcranial Doppler ultrasonography to assess cerebral blood flow velocity and guide blood pressure management in patients with acute brain injury. Doppler-derived parameters can help identify pressure ranges that favor cerebral perfusion. This approach is part of a multimodal monitoring strategy.

item.title: Incidence of Dependency-Related Skin Injury in Critical Care: A Longitudinal Study.
item.description: This study found that 33.1% of critically ill patients developed dependency-related skin injuries, with pressure ulcers being the most common type. The use of medical devices and high-risk scores on risk assessment scales increased the likelihood of these injuries. The mean time to injury onset was 9.2 days.

item.title: Remote Multicomponent Rehabilitation in Intensive Care Unit Survivors: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.description: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week remote rehabilitation program on health-related quality of life in ICU survivors who required mechanical ventilation. The program included symptom management, exercise, and psychological support. The results showed no significant improvement in health-related quality of life at 8 weeks compared to standard care.

item.title: Explainable machine learning model for early prediction of ICU death in chronic heart failure with pulmonary infection.
item.description: Researchers developed and validated a machine learning model using the XGBoost algorithm to predict ICU death in patients with chronic heart failure and pulmonary infection. The model was able to identify key predictors of mortality, including lactic acid, white blood cell count, and pre-existing diabetes. The model's performance was evaluated and found to be accurate in predicting ICU mortality.

item.title: HFNC vs. NIV in Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema: Go with the Flow?
item.description: This study compared high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) to non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in patients with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema. It found that HFNC may be as effective as NIV in reducing respiratory rate and improving respiratory distress within 2 hours. The study aimed to determine if HFNC is a viable alternative to NIV in this setting.

item.title: ECG criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy
item.description: This study reviews the ECG criteria for diagnosing left ventricular hypertrophy, including their historical development, diagnostic performance, and limitations. It aims to provide a comprehensive overview of these criteria for clinicians. The study covers the principal ECG criteria used to diagnose left ventricular hypertrophy.

item.title: Use of Sedation During Non-Invasive Ventilation in Intensive Care Unit: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies found that sedation, especially with dexmedetomidine, may improve non-invasive ventilation success and reduce the need for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. However, dexmedetomidine was also associated with higher rates of bradycardia and hypotension. The optimal sedation strategy depends on the patient's individual needs and risk factors.

item.title: Prognostic impact of sepsis-induced coagulopathy on mortality and clinical outcomes in ICU patients.
item.description: This study found that sepsis-induced coagulopathy is associated with higher in-hospital mortality and increased need for vasopressor support in ICU patients with sepsis. The study used a scoring system to predict mortality, which showed moderate discriminative performance. The results suggest that sepsis-induced coagulopathy may provide additional prognostic information when used alongside existing severity assessment tools.

item.title: The Case of the Malignant Cohort
item.description: The YEARS protocol was tested to see if it can safely identify low-risk patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. The study aimed to determine if this approach can be applied to patients with malignancy. Results were not provided.

item.title: High-Dose Intravenous Vitamin C in Critical Illness: A Translational Exposure-Response Framework for Biomarker-Guided Precision Therapy.
item.description: This study explores the use of high-dose intravenous vitamin C as a potential therapy in critical illness, finding that plasma concentrations and timing of administration may influence its effectiveness. Biomarkers can be used to guide treatment and monitor response. The study suggests a shift towards precision-based therapy.

item.title: The interplay between early energy intake and nosocomial infection risk in the critically ill neonate.
item.description: Researchers studied 200 critically ill neonates to see if early nutrition affects the risk of hospital-acquired infections. They found that achieving energy targets early on reduced the risk of infection, especially in very low birth weight infants.

item.title: A distributional reinforcement learning model for temporal coagulation balance evaluation and state‑guided supportive suggestions.
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model to help manage bleeding and clotting in critically ill patients by analyzing their medical records and lab results. The model showed promise in guiding personalized treatment and identifying key factors that affect bleeding and clotting. It can help doctors make more informed decisions about patient care.

item.title: EMCrit RACC-Lit Review – 2026 July
item.description: This is a literature review on various topics in critical care, including prehospital whole blood transfusions, defibrillator damage from DSD, and adenosine dosing for supraventricular tachycardia.

item.title: Vasopressor Dosing Trajectories in Septic Shock According to Initial Antimicrobial Susceptibility and Infection Source Concordance: A Retrospective Observational Study.
item.description: This study looked at how vasopressor dosing changed in patients with septic shock based on whether their initial antibiotic therapy was effective and matched the actual infection source. They found that patients who received appropriate antibiotic therapy had shorter and more rapid vasopressor reduction. This could help clinicians identify when to reassess antibiotic therapy and infection source evaluation.

item.title: Timing of disseminated intravascular coagulation onset is associated with development of persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome in critically ill patients.
item.description: Researchers studied 100 ICU patients to see if disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is linked to a condition called persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome (PIICS). They found that DIC occurring after 8 days in the ICU may increase the risk of PIICS. The study suggests that coagulopathy during the middle phase of ICU stay may contribute to PIICS.

item.title: Beyond Description: A Functional GIUS-Based Algorithm for Enteral Feeding Decisions in the ICU.
item.description: This study reviewed existing methods for assessing gastrointestinal function in ICU patients and proposed algorithms for enteral feeding decisions using gastrointestinal ultrasound. It found that certain sonographic parameters, like gastric antral cross-sectional area, are clinically relevant. The study suggests that GIUS-based algorithms may improve enteral nutrition management but more research is needed.

item.title: Can’t Intubate Can’t Oxygenate (CICO)
item.description: This study discusses the management of Can't Intubate Can't Oxygenate (CICO) situations in ICU, where standard airway rescue techniques fail. CICO is recognized, and the patient is prepared for Front of Neck Access (FONA). FONA is then transitioned to for oxygen delivery.

item.title: Adult Intubation Checklist
item.description: This study developed a checklist for adult intubation in emergency situations, covering preparation, pause before intubation, backup plans, and post-intubation care. The checklist aims to standardize and improve the intubation process. It may reduce errors and improve patient outcomes.

item.title: EMCrit 429 – RUSH 2.0 – The I-RUSH and CRUSH Exams
item.description: This episode introduces the updated RUSH Exam 2.0, also known as the iRUSH, which provides a standardized map for comprehensive bedside hemodynamic assessment. It combines clinical findings with advanced ultrasound modalities to phenotype shock. This updated protocol moves beyond its original role for the crashing patient.

item.title: Anatomy for bronchoscopy
item.description: This study reviews airway anatomy to help clinicians understand the basics of bronchoscopy and airway management, highlighting normal variations and potential abnormalities.

item.title: Nutrition Therapy in Critically Ill Adults.
item.description: Critically ill adults experience severe muscle loss and gut dysfunction. Early nutrition therapy can support gut health, but full-dose energy delivery may increase complications. A restrictive nutrition strategy is recommended, especially in patients with circulatory shock or refeeding syndrome risk.

item.title: Agreement of Electrolyte Measurements Between Arterial Blood Gas Analyzers and Central Laboratories in Critically Ill Patients with Acute Kidney Injury.
item.description: This study compared electrolyte measurements from arterial blood gas (ABG) analyzers to central laboratory analyzers in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). The results showed relatively good agreement for sodium and potassium measurements, but clinically meaningful discrepancies occurred in a subset of measurements.
